metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Planten Park & Brown Ave District, North 8th & Fairview Heights
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 6.231%, with an equalization ratio of 46.75%.
Public education represents 52.8% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 31.9%.
Average residential assessment is $184,663, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,506.35.

neighborhoods.name: Planten Park & Brown Ave District
neighborhoods.character: Compact residential borough bordering Planten Park and Paterson, with two-family frame homes and single-family dwellings
neighborhoods.description: Dense 0.48-square-mile borough offering close-knit neighborhood character adjacent to Planten Park recreation.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Certified tax rate of 5.122% reflects compact residential ratables with minimal commercial space.

neighborhoods.name: North 8th & Fairview Heights
neighborhoods.character: Elevated residential section overlooking Passaic Valley with single-family homes, duplexes, and quiet streets
neighborhoods.description: Family-oriented residential blocks convenient to School No. 1 and local neighborhood parks.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Compact tax base with close municipal expenditure controls.

equityAnalysis.summary: Prospect Park Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Prospect Park Borough, homeowners pay an average of $11,506.35 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 14.98% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 46.75%, assessed values average ~46.75% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 52.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 31.9%, and Passaic County claims 15.3%.
